## Overview
The Clinic Management System manages patient admissions, electronic medical records (EMR), scheduling, and billing for medium-sized hospitals and clinics. It operates as a hybrid architecture ensuring high availability and strict regulatory compliance.

## Key Elements
* Front Desk Staff, Clinicians, Billing Officers, Patients, and Regulatory Auditors
* Clinic Management System (internal hybrid software system)
* Identity Provider (OIDC/SAML)
* External Lab & Imaging Systems (HL7 FHIR)
* Third-Party Payment Gateway & Insurance Clearinghouse
* Centralized SIEM & Observability Platform
* Global Traffic Manager / Anycast DNS
* Distributed Network Interconnect / SD-WAN

## Relationships
* Users interact with the Clinic Management System via HTTPS and OIDC
* Clinic Management System integrates with Lab & Imaging Systems via HL7 FHIR over HTTPS
* Clinic Management System connects to Payment Gateway & Insurance Clearinghouse via REST over HTTPS
* Services communicate across the hybrid boundary using mTLS with SPIFFE/SPIRE identities
* Telemetry and audit logs stream to the SIEM Platform via secure syslog/OTLP with PHI masking

## Technology Stack
* Kubernetes (`on-prem-k8s`) and AWS (`eu-central-1`) for hybrid cloud deployment
* TLS 1.3 and mTLS for all network transport security
* AES-256 for data at rest, managed via on-prem Hardware Security Modules (HSMs) and AWS KMS
* OIDC/SAML for multi-factor authentication and identity federation
* DNSSEC and Anycast DNS for traffic routing and DDoS mitigation

## Rationale
This architecture satisfies high availability and sub-second performance SLAs through active-active hybrid redundancy and global traffic management. It enforces HIPAA and GDPR compliance via zero-trust boundaries, robust encryption, and centralized audit logging.

## Overview
The Clinic Management System is a hybrid cloud platform designed to manage patient admissions, electronic medical records (EMR), scheduling, and billing for medium-sized hospitals and clinics. It ensures HIPAA/GDPR compliance, 99.99% availability, and strict data retention policies.

## Key Elements
- **Users**: Front Desk Staff, Clinicians, Billing Officers, Patients, Regulatory Auditors
- **Clients**: React Single-Page Application (SPA) / React Native Mobile Client
- **Edge Layer**: Envoy API Gateway / Edge Proxy
- **Core Services**: EMR & Scheduling Service (Node.js/Java), Billing & Claims Service (Java), FHIR Interoperability Service (HAPI FHIR)
- **Data & Messaging Tier**: Region-local PostgreSQL databases, localized Apache Kafka/RabbitMQ message brokers, AWS S3 / on-prem object storage (WORM)
- **Infrastructure & Security**: Kubernetes (`on-prem-k8s`, `eu-central-1`), Istio/Linkerd Service Mesh, HashiCorp Vault, Centralized SIEM

## Relationships
- Clients interact with the Envoy API Gateway via HTTPS/TLS 1.3 using OAuth2/OIDC validation.
- Envoy routes requests to internal containers using internal mTLS via Istio/Linkerd.
- EMR and Billing services connect to region-local PostgreSQL instances via encrypted TCP.
- FHIR Interoperability Service communicates asynchronously with backend services via Apache Kafka/RabbitMQ using W3C Trace Context headers.
- Services retrieve secrets dynamically from HashiCorp Vault.

## Technology Stack
- **Frontend**: React and React Native delivered via CDN for optimized client rendering.
- **Backend**: Node.js/TypeScript and Java/Spring Boot containers optimized for sub-second responses.
- **Database & Storage**: PostgreSQL for regional operational storage; S3-compatible object storage with WORM policies for 10-year audit retention.
- **Messaging**: Apache Kafka or RabbitMQ for asynchronous, decoupled data exchanges.
- **Infrastructure & Security**: Kubernetes orchestrated via ArgoCD, Istio/Linkerd for mTLS, HashiCorp Vault for secrets management, and OpenTelemetry for observability.

## Rationale
The hybrid architecture utilizes region-local primary databases and asynchronous messaging to prevent wide-area network latency, ensuring sub-second EMR load times and 99.99% availability. Strict container isolation, mTLS, AES-256 encryption, and immutable audit logs satisfy rigorous HIPAA, GDPR, and financial compliance mandates.

• PostgreSQL: Handles persistent structured storage with AES-256 encryption at rest.
• React and React Native: Powers cross-platform client presentation layers.

## Rationale
• The hybrid deployment with independent regional Vault clusters and Enterprise Performance Replication prevents wide-area network partitions and guarantees 99.99% uptime.
• Automated 30-day credential rotation, strict path-based ACLs, and Transit envelope encryption satisfy rigorous HIPAA and GDPR compliance standards.
